Ilia Begichev, Daria Belotcerkovtceva, Iakov Reznikov, Sergey Slizovskiy, Weijie Lu, Nansi Zhou, Ian Babich, Makars Šiškins, et al.
Encapsulation of two-dimensional (2D) materials with hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is widely used to fabricate ultraclean van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures for optoelectronic and quantum transport studies. These devices are often operated under strong out-of-plane displacement fields that tune the electronic properties of the active 2D material, while the surrounding hBN is typically assumed to remain electronically inert. This assumption, however, neglects defect states that are present even in high-quality hBN crystals. Here, we probe their response to the applied displacement field using monolayer graphene encapsulated between hBN crystals as a sensitive charge sensor. Increasing the displacement field induces notable charge transfer between graphene and hBN, producing additional electron doping of ≈10–20 × 109 cm–2 even at the moderate displacement field (∼0.5 V nm–1), while simultaneously increasing carrier-density inhomogeneity of the graphene layer. Both effects are consistent with ionization of defect states within the hBN bandgap, with the bulk density ∼1–7 × 10–5 nm–3 varying across different hBN crystals. Our results show that displacement-field-induced defect ionization in hBN can modify the electronic response of vdW heterostructures, with direct implications for device design and interpretation of experiments.

item.title: Nano Letters: Direct Experimental Quantification of Intrinsic Capacitive Properties of Monolayer Ti3C2T x MXene
item.description:
Minghao Xu, Qingfeng Wu, Sixing Xu, Xiaohong Wang
Ti3C2Tx MXene is widely employed in energy storage because of its unique interfacial charge-storage properties. Understanding its intrinsic capacitive properties, especially the surface characteristics of a monolayer flake, is critical to optimizing device performance, but direct measurement at the monolayer level remains elusive. Here, we report, for the first time, direct experimental quantification of the intrinsic capacitance of monolayer Ti3C2Tx MXene by integrating optimized flake protection and parasitic-capacitance-shielding strategies. The quasi-static areal capacitance is 141 μF cm–2 in acidic electrolytes and 61–74 μF cm–2 in alkali-metal-ion electrolytes. Decoupling the pseudocapacitive and electric-double-layer contributions by resolving the concentration dependence reveals that pseudocapacitance accounts for ∼45% of the total in acidic electrolytes but <10% in alkali-metal-ion electrolytes. Temperature-dependent kinetics show that a lower proton-transfer activation energy facilitates the pseudocapacitive charge storage. This work quantifies how redox and double-layer mechanisms coexist on a monolayer Ti3C2Tx MXene surface and establishes a benchmark across the field.

item.title: Nano Letters: A Golgi-Targeted Cu-MOF Nanoplatform Overcomes ATP7B-Mediated Copper Efflux to Amplify Chemo–Cuproptosis Synergy against Colorectal Cancer
item.description:
Mengyuan He, Aixue Li, Rongchen Mao, Lingtao Kong, Xuejun Wang, Xiaoli Cheng, Gou Wu, Wenxin Zhang, et al.
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains difficult to treat because of tumor heterogeneity and an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Although combining chemotherapy with cuproptosis offers complementary antitumor effects, its efficacy is constrained by poor tumor-selective delivery and ATP7B-associated copper efflux. We developed YC@BS-MOF, a yuanhuacine (YC)-loaded copper metal–organic framework (MOF) with Golgi-targeting capability, to integrate chemotherapy, photodynamic therapy, and cuproptosis. Composed of Cu2+ nodes and Golgi-targeting BS-TCPP photosensitizing ligands, BS-MOF acted as a copper reservoir and, upon light irradiation, induced Golgi disruption that impaired ATP7B-associated Cu handling and promoted intracellular copper retention. Copper retention amplified YC-mediated apoptosis and copper-dependent oxidative stress, leading to enhanced cuproptosis, immunogenic cell death, and activation of the immune microenvironment. Biodistribution analyses showed increased YC tumor accumulation, and in vivo studies demonstrated potent tumor suppression, immune remodeling, and favorable biosafety. This work establishes Golgi-directed regulation of copper trafficking as a subcellular strategy to potentiate chemo–cuproptosis for CRC treatment.

item.title: JACS: One-Pot Hierarchical Assembly of Simple Molecules to Vinylene- and Indole-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks
item.description:
Jie-Min Chen, Chao-Ran Qi, Yu-Bao Lan, Jing Han, Guan-Le Chen, Er-Duo Yu, Muzaffar Ali Khan, Zhi-Peng Wang, et al.
The development in the synthesis of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) has been oriented toward the integration of simplicity, accessibility, stability, diversity, and functionality. However, a central bottleneck remains the lack of effective strategies for assembling simple, unsymmetric, and readily available molecules into highly ordered frameworks. Here, we report a practical synthesis of robust, diversified, and functional COFs via one-pot assembly from a low-cost and simple-structured molecule, 4-methyl-3-nitrobenzonitrile (MNBN). Leveraging the versatile but orthogonal reactivities of MNBN, a three-step cascade sequence, including nitrile cyclotrimerization, Knoevenagel condensation, and reductive cyclization, achieved the symmetrization, reticulation, and functionalization in one pot, thereby enabling the hierarchical construction of two series of COFs with stable o-nitrostyrene or indole linkages. The resulting COFs displayed high crystallinity, permanent porosity, and exceptional stability; solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (SSNMR) experiments combined with selective isotopic-labeling synthesis further confirmed the high selectivity and controllability of the hierarchical assembly. Notably, the indole-linked COFs, featuring conjugated and electron-rich frameworks, displayed emergent photoelectronic properties and served as efficient, reusable catalysts in both metal-free photocatalytic and metallaphotoredox reactions. By hierarchically exploiting the intrinsic reactivity of a simple, unsymmetric molecule, this work bridges classical organic synthesis and cross-scale covalent assembly, achieving the programmable construction of stable, diversified, and functional COFs.

item.title: ACS Nano: Riveting Rubidium in Alkali-Metal Layers: High-Performance P2-Type Layered Oxide Cathodes for Potassium-Ion Batteries
item.description:
Liping Duan, Yichen Du, Qixiang Huang, Zeyu Yuan, Zicheng Wu, Chi Zhou, Yumiao Ruan, Xiaosi Zhou
Layered manganese-based oxides for potassium-ion batteries (PIBs) suffer from severe structural degradation, primarily due to irreversible phase transitions, Jahn–Teller distortion, and sluggish K+ diffusion kinetics. Here, we propose an alkali-metal site riveting strategy by selectively incorporating oversized Rb+ ions into the prismatic sites of P2-type K0.55Mn0.8Ni0.1T0.1O2. The introduced Rb+ acts as a rigid pillar, expanding the interlayer spacing and reinforcing adjacent transition-metal–oxygen (TM–O) bonds. This synergistic modulation not only widens the two-dimensional diffusion channels for rapid K+ transport but also effectively suppresses the detrimental P2–P′2 phase transition and mitigates Jahn–Teller distortion of Mn3+. Consequently, the optimized K0.55Rb0.025Mn0.8Ni0.1Ti0.1O2 cathode delivers a high reversible capacity of 105.3 mAh g–1 at a current density of 20 mA g–1, outstanding rate capability (56.1 mAh g–1 at 500 mA g–1), and long-term cycling stability with 82.1% capacity retention after 500 cycles. Furthermore, a pouch cell paired with a soft carbon anode achieves 81.3% capacity retention over 300 cycles. This work demonstrates that anchoring oversized cations in alkali-metal layers provides a universal and effective strategy toward near-zero-strain layered oxide cathodes for advanced PIBs.

item.title: ACS Nano: Visualizing Single-Cell Secretion with Electrochemiluminescence Imaging
item.description:
Langxia Feng, Binxiao Li, Xuedong Huang, Yujun Ning, Ruolin Yang, Baohong Liu
Secretory proteins encode cellular states not only through their abundance but also through their intracellular transport before being released. However, visualizing protein secretion behavior with molecular specificity and a low background remains challenging. Here, we report VEGF-responsive electrochemiluminescence (ECL) nanoemitters that enable spatiotemporal mapping of intracellular protein distribution at different stages of the secretion process by integrating a metal–organic framework (MOF) confining Ru(bpy)32+ with DNA tetrahedral gates (DTGs) programmed with aptamers. The MOF core provides bright, stable, and electrically addressable ECL emission, whereas the discrete DTGs regulate coreactant accessibility and prevent premature emission until VEGF recognition triggers gate displacement and restores ECL activity, converting intracellular molecular recognition events to quantitative optical signals. This architecture enables rapid, concentration-dependent, and selective activation, allowing high contrast discrimination of VEGF-rich tumor cells from epithelial cells. Under DFO stimulation, single-cell ECL imaging revealed heterogeneous VEGF upregulation and mapped its progressive redistribution from the perinuclear region to the cell periphery during secretion. This gated ECL platform enables quantitative spatiotemporal visualization of protein secretion behavior beyond the static molecular localization.

item.title: ACS Nano: Flexible Nanofibrous Membrane with Valley-Cell Array of Rapid Thermal Response and Stability for Efficient Water Harvesting Performance
item.description:
Huijie Wei, Lingmei Zhu, Tiance Zhang, Boyang Tian, Jianhua Wang, Chen Yang, Yongping Hou, Yongmei Zheng
We demonstrate a flexible nanofibrous membrane featuring a valley-cell array (NMVA). Inspired by honeycombs and spider silk, the NMVA is rationally designed using poly(vinyl alcohol), carbon black, and MOF-303 as its main components. The synergistic effect of the flexible honeycomb network, abundant hydrophilic sites of MOF-decorated nanofibers, rapid photothermal response, and multidimensional structural stability favors highly efficient adsorption and desorption dynamics during water harvesting. The valleys of the honeycomb cell arrays enhance light capture for photothermal conversion and water release, while the abundant hydrophilic sites facilitate water molecule capture and uptake. As a result, NMVA achieves a high water uptake capacity of ∼0.41 g g–1 at 25 °C and 30% RH, and can release 92% of the absorbed water within 30 min under 1 sun irradiation. For an integrated NMVA in outdoor conditions under sunlight of ∼0.76 kW m–2 on average, water harvesting capacities reach 3.85–5.0 L kg–1 day–1 at 42–68% RH through continuous all-day water uptake–release over seven cycles. This study provides insights into the design of novel materials that can be extended into the realms of water engineering for energy systems and portable devices.

item.title: JACS: A Dynamic Self-Reporting Metal–Organic Framework System for Catalysis and Real-Time Reaction Monitoring
item.description:
Jiatong Huo, Zongsu Han, Wenxuan Li, Yihao Yang, Zekihan Ozerdem, Narasimhan Loganathan, Xincheng Liu, Joshua Rushlow, et al.
Modern catalysis research has primarily focused on improving catalyst activity, selectivity, and stability through active-site engineering, microenvironment regulation, and mechanistic understanding. However, the sustainability and efficiency of catalytic processes also depend on the dynamic evolution of reaction systems, including substrate consumption, catalyst deactivation, and product accumulation. Despite their importance, these changes are typically assessed by off-line analysis rather than real-time monitoring, which hinders efficient process optimization and sustainable operation. Here, we develop a dynamic self-reporting (DSR) catalytic system based on Ag@UiO-66-(COOH)2/NDCA that simultaneously functions as a heterogeneous oxidation catalyst and an optical reporter for reaction progress. During oxidation, the emission intensity at 440 nm increases with product formation and exhibits a strong quantitative correlation with benzaldehyde yield, enabling reaction progress to be continuously tracked across a series of substituted benzyl alcohols. Mechanistic studies indicate that the luminescence response is governed by competitive absorption and substrate-dependent interactions. Density functional theory calculations further reveal that benzyl alcohol forms stronger dispersion-stabilized π···π interactions with the emissive NDCA2– linkers than benzaldehyde, resulting in more pronounced luminescence quenching. As benzyl alcohol is converted into the more weakly interacting product, this quenching is progressively relieved, producing a measurable increase in emission intensity that reports the reaction progress. This integration provides a platform for reaction monitoring, process optimization, and future automated manufacturing.

item.title: Nano Letters: The Role of Atomistic Tip Morphology in Tip-Enhanced Electronic Energy Transfer
item.description:
Pablo Grobas Illobre, Sveva Sodomaco, Piero Lafiosca, Tommaso Giovannini, Chiara Cappelli
Tip-enhanced photoluminescence in scanning tunneling microscopy nanocavities has emerged as a powerful tool to probe intermolecular electronic energy transfer (EET) at the single-molecule level. Single-atom modifications at a metallic tip apex can drastically alter the near-field, yet their quantitative impact on intermolecular EET has remained elusive. By exploiting a multiscale fully atomistic quantum mechanical (QM)/electrodynamical approach, we show a nontrivial modulation of the EET-driven fluorescence, jointly determined by the atomistic morphology and single-atom features of the silver tip apex. Remarkably, we demonstrate that a fully atomistic QM/Classical description, able to treat systems of more than ten thousand atoms, is essential to capture how subtle apex rearrangements affect intermolecular EET. Our results quantitatively reproduce experimental fluorescence spectra and Förster-type distance behaviors, providing a direct structure–property connection at the atomistic level, crucial for predictive simulations of tip-enhanced spectroscopies.

item.title: JACS: Luminescent Timeline from Confined Active Radicals Enables Infinite Cryptograph
item.description:
Haomin Li, Juzhong Zhang, Jiajun Qi, Tianfu Song, Haifeng Yu
The development of encryption materials is essential to meeting the increasing demand for information security. However, the present materials are susceptible to duplication due to a finite numbers of crypto states. Here, we report one chemical method to expand anticounterfeiting information from discrete, finite states to continuous, infinite states in the temporal domain by regulating the chemical reactions of luminescent radicals with the assistance of image-analysis technology. Infinite cryptographic materials were fabricated with continuous dynamic luminescence processes by integrating reversible radical reactions into confined radical luminescent systems. The inherent chemical kinetics of active radical emitters can be converted to time-dependent emission curves, serving as unclonable keys with nearly infinite crypto states in the temporal domain. Fluorescent AIE molecules were then introduced to expand the color gamut, further enriching the encoding capacity. These infinite cryptographic materials offer a robust anticounterfeiting platform, providing novel pathways for high-level information-protection applications.

item.title: JACS: Protecting Groups as Catalysts: Direct Synthesis of Primary Amines from Ammonia under Carbonyl Catalysis
item.description:
Kazuki Shimozono, Nao Nishimoto, Takuma Tagami, Takashi Ohshima
Primary amines are indispensable building blocks in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials, yet their direct, modular synthesis from ammonia remains challenging. Here we report a carbonyl catalysis strategy that enables the direct synthesis of structurally complex primary amines from ammonia by integrating the conventional multistep sequence of protection, N–H functionalization, and deprotection into a single catalytic cycle. As a proof of concept, amino-trifluoromethylation of alkenes using ammonium salts and Togni reagent afforded a wide range of β-trifluoromethylated primary amines, including derivatives of complex natural products. 1,8-Diazafluorenone was uniquely competent as a carbonyl catalyst, highlighting the critical role of catalyst design in ammonia transformation. Mechanistic studies suggest that its distinctive electronic structure facilitates the formation of the N–H ketimine intermediate, a prerequisite for catalytic turnover. These findings establish carbonyl catalysis as a platform for the direct transformation of ammonia and demonstrate how protecting groups can function as catalysts.

item.title: JACS: Complementary Acetonitrile Reduction and Amine Adsorption on Mixed Cu–Ni Oxides for Electrocatalytic N-Ethylation
item.description:
Yuping Pan, Yangyang Zou, Zhuoran Lu, Dianke Xie, Ta Thi Thuy Nga, Zhongcheng Xia, Chung-Li Dong, Shuangyin Wang, et al.
N-ethylamines are important motifs in pharmaceuticals and fine chemicals, but their selective synthesis from nitriles requires control over both nitrile reduction and amine availability at the catalyst-electrolyte interface. Herein, we investigate mixed Cu–Ni oxides for the aqueous electrocatalytic C–N coupling of acetonitrile (MeCN) with benzylamine (BA). The optimized Cu-NiO-0.5 catalyst affords N-ethylbenzylamine (EBA) in 75% yield with 87% selectivity and a mass-normalized formation rate of 12.5 mmol h–1 gcat–1 at −0.5 VRHE. Electrochemical testing indicates that the presence of CuO can promote the MeCN electrochemical reduction, generating abundant ethylimine for subsequent coupling. Meanwhile, the incorporation of Ni significantly enhances the adsorption of BA, accelerating the C–N coupling between the ethylimine and BA. In situ experimental measurements further confirm the sequential reduction-condensation-reduction pathway. Moreover, this strategy has also been proven to enable efficient C–N coupling between MeCN and various amine derivatives, giving the corresponding N-ethylated products in 58.3–84.6% yield and greater than 74% selectivity. This work offers an environmentally friendly strategy for the electrocatalytic synthesis of N-ethylamines.

item.title: Nano Letters: Direct Restoration of Spent LiFePO4 via Lattice Defect Correction and Nitrogen-Doped Interface Engineering
item.description:
Xutao Liang, Yang Gao, Jiping Ma, Ran Wang, Zelin Lv, Xiaoxiao Li, Yongle Yan, Lifeng Hou, et al.
The proliferation of spent lithium-ion batteries demands efficient, environmentally sustainable recycling technologies, yet regenerating spent cathode materials remains challenging. Here, we present a mild, scalable direct regeneration strategy for spent LiFePO4 (S-LFP) cathodes leveraging the synergistic effect of ethanolamine and LiNO3. Ethanolamine with moderate alkalinity and strong reducing capability gently removes surface passivation layers and amorphous impurities, selectively reducing Fe(III) to Fe(II) for lattice-stabilized valence balance. Thanks to its low steric hindrance and favorable mass-transport properties, it penetrates particle interiors and cooperates with Li+ from LiNO3 to fill Li vacancies, eliminating Li–Fe antisite defects and repairing distorted lattices. During subsequent annealing, ethanolamine acts as an in situ N source to form a uniform N-doped interfacial layer that suppresses side reactions and boosts charge-transfer kinetics. Regenerated LiFePO4 (R-LFP) achieves 106.04 mAh g–1 at 5.0 C with 100% capacity retention over 500 cycles. EverBatt-based assessments confirm its favorable economic and environmental benefits.

item.title: Nano Letters: Unraveling the Effect of Tensile Strain on Electrochemical CO2 Reduction
item.description:
Qing Yuan, Chengdi Huang, Xuan Yang
Introducing tensile strain into copper-based (Cu-based) catalysts is a promising strategy for improving the performance of the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). However, isolating the influence of the strain effect remains challenging owing to the convoluted contributions from grain boundaries, ligands, and facets. Herein, we utilize in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) to isolate the effect of strain on the CO2RR performance and determine the strain–activity correlations by taking advantage of synthesizing colloidal nanoparticles with well-defined structures. Tensile strain is shown to modulate CO2RR performance by tuning the CO binding strength of the Cu-based catalysts. Medium tensile strain leads to moderate CO adsorption, which is beneficial for the formation of multicarbon products. Excessively strong CO adsorption would instead hinder the CO2RR and promote the hydrogen evolution reaction. This work provides experimental evidence for the rational design of high-performance CO2RR catalysts to produce C2+ products via strain engineering.

item.title: JACS: A Stable Phosphinidene Radical Anion as a Multielectron Reducing Agent
item.description:
Yizhen Chen, Lu Zhang, Xinyi Li, Lei Xu, Zheng Liu, Hansjörg Grützmacher, Song Gao, Gengwen Tan
The diagonal relationship between carbon and phosphorus has long inspired comparisons between the chemistries of carbenes and phosphinidenes. However, while carbene chemistry has flourished over the past three decades, isolable phosphinidenes remain exceptionally rare, and their one-electron reduction products, phosphinidene radical anions, are unknown. Here, we report the synthesis and isolation of a crystalline phosphinidene radical anion through one-electron reduction of a ring-strained phosphanorcaradiene, a phosphinidene equivalent. Structural, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal a monocoordinate phosphorus center where the unpaired electron is predominantly localized, in line with a highly reduced phosphorus center. The radical anion exhibits multielectron redox reactivity, including radical addition to an arylalkyne, sulfur atom transfer from isothiocyanate, elemental chalcogen activation, and stepwise oxidation to high-valent P(V) compounds through an overall five-electron process, integrating formal paramagnetic P(0)/P(II)/P(IV) radicals and diamagnetic P(I)/P(III)/P(V) derivatives.

item.title: JACS: Cooperative Enantiomorphic-Site and Chain-End Chirality in Isoselective β-Lactone Polymerization
item.description:
Morgan S. Young, Yolanda Rusconi, Ethan B. Flanagan, Samantha N. MacMillan, Claudio De Rosa, Anne M. LaPointe, Giovanni Talarico, Geoffrey W. Coates
Polymer properties are profoundly impacted by tacticity, necessitating an understanding of the origins of stereocontrol to make high-performance materials. Recently, we reported that controlled incorporation of stereoerrors into trans-poly(3-hydroxy-2-methylbutyrate) (trans-PHMB) through the isoselective polymerization of rac-trans-3,4-dimethylpropiolactone (trans-DMPL) using racemic “sandwich” (BDI)Zn alkoxide complexes (where BDI = β-diketiminate) enables tuning of mechanical properties to match those of low-density polyethylene. However, the mechanism of stereocontrol of these catalysts was not explored. Herein, we report a thorough experimental and computational investigation uncovering a distinct manifestation of cooperative enantiomorphic-site and chain-end control, which we describe as site-mediated asymmetric chain-end control, where catalyst (Δ and Λ) and chain-end chiralities (R,R or S,S) work synergistically to influence the reaction’s stereoselectivity and rate. Experimental and computational data converge remarkably well, revealing that a Δ-catalyst with an (R,R)-chain end (Δ-RR) is isoselective 90% of the time. In contrast, a Δ-catalyst with an (S,S)-chain end (Δ-SS) is unselective. Detailed Density Functional Theory (DFT) investigations suggest molecular-level rationale for this mechanism of stereocontrol, demonstrating that chain positioning, monomer distortion, and ligand interactions work in conjunction to foster isoselectivity. Finally, DFT and kinetic modeling reveal that when polymerizing rac-trans-DMPL, the populations of Δ-RR and Δ-SS are equal and the high overall isoselectivity (mm% = 71–73%; where mm% is the percent of triads with a meso configuration across both ester linkages) of the catalyst is attributed to Δ-RR being faster than Δ-SS.

item.title: Nano Letters: Ultrafast Mimic of Spin Hall Effect in Altermagnets
item.description:
Ruikai Wu, Deepika Gill, Wenhan Chen, Peter Elliott, Sangeeta Sharma, Sam Shallcross
The spin Hall effect, a key effect in creating spin currents and controlling magnetic order at the nanoscale, presupposes a population of mobile carriers in a conducting state, in which a driving charge current generates a perpendicular spin-current. Here we show an ultrafast light-wave driven spin Hall analogue exists in altermagnetic semiconductors and insulators, in which a laser pulse generates both a charge current and a co-occurring perpendicular pure spin current. Employing the example of the theoretically predicted 2d altermagnetic Lieb-lattice semiconductor Cr2SO, we demonstrate that pulse design allows lightwave control over the postpulse spin/charge current ratio ξres, with values exceeding unity obtained in the multicycle regime. Our findings thus both considerably broaden the materials base for spin Hall/spin splitter physics, as well as establishing 2d altermagnets as a platform providing a new route for valleytronic lightwave control of spin- and charge currents at ultrafast times.

item.title: Nano Letters: Mica–Polyethylenimine Membranes for High-Efficiency pH-Responsive Nanofiltration Enabled by a Strongly Coupled Charge Flip
item.description:
Mingbo Xie, Huacun Li, Yeqiu Zhao, Jingjing Deng, Jinkang Liu, Xu Yan, Qingwei Wang, Meiqing Shi, et al.
The pH-responsive two-dimensional nanofiltration membranes enable tunable separation, yet existing membranes suffer from weak charge gating. Herein, we prepared a mica–polyethylenimine membrane using a “coupled charge flip” strategy. The membrane exhibits a strong charge flip (zeta potential from +46.1 to −36.4 mV) across pH 2–12, originating from the synergy between polyethylenimine (zeta potential from +35.2 to +2.5 mV) and mica (zeta potential from −3.1 to −55.7 mV), yielding a charge-flip amplitude (82.5 mV) 41% greater than that of the best performing bipolar pH-responsive membranes. This enables superior pH-dependent molecular gating (e.g., methyl orange) with rejection ranging from 96.98 to 5.03% (pH 2–12) and a gating ratio of 19.28, which is 1.76 times that of the best reported pH-responsive membranes, while maintaining a water permeance of 155 L m–2 h–1 bar–1 and stable cycling over eight pH switches. This work provides a new framework for designing pH-responsive nanofiltration membranes with high gating ratios.

item.title: ACS Nano: Nanoedge-Regulated Impedance Sensing for Sensitive Cardiomyocyte Mechanophysiological Investigation and Functional Drug Assessment
item.description:
Chengyun Wang, Jiaru Fang, Hao Wang, Zhekun Jia, Tao Liang, Dongxin Xu, Ning Hu, Zhen Wang
Cardiomyocyte contraction drives the pumping action of the heart and is fundamental to cardiac mechanophysiology research. Conventional optical and force-based approaches for cardiomyocyte contraction detection are limited by phototoxicity or potential alterations in cell morphology and physiology. Electrical impedance sensing is a label-free approach for noninvasive contraction recording, but current sensor optimization still mainly relies on substantial adjustments to electrode size or pattern. Herein, we present a nanoedge-regulated impedance sensing (NERIS) approach. Electrode structures with different pit depths are designed to regulate the cell-electrode interface to precisely optimize impedance properties. Increasing pit depth shifts the peak impedance response to lower frequencies, potentially reducing detection system bandwidth demands. At the optimized frequencies, long-term recordings support quantitative analysis of cardiomyocyte mechanophysiology. Furthermore, functional cardiac drug assessment is performed by characterizing contractile responses to norepinephrine and isradipine. This NERIS approach is expected to be widely applied in cardiomyocyte mechanophysiology and cardiac drug assessment.

item.title: JACS: Perfluoroalkyl Anion Strategy to Construct Anion–π+ Type NIR-II Phototheranostic Agents for Enhanced Tumor Immunotherapy via Necroptosis/Ferroptosis
item.description:
Lingxiu Liu, Xue Wang, Jianye Gong, Ying Zhang, Guoyu Jiang, Ben Zhong Tang, Jianguo Wang
Anion-π+ photosensitizers (PSs) possess exceptional reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and precise organelle targeting that could disrupt intracellular metabolic homeostasis and induce nonapoptotic cell death, offering unique advantages in overcoming immunosuppression. However, previous reports mainly focused on modifying the π+ core but often overlooked the crucial role of anions. Herein, we present a facile perfluoroalkyl anion strategy to modulate the fluorescence intensity and ROS generation capacity of anion-π+ PSs. Perfluorobutanesulfonate (PFB) anions with a single-sided perfluoroalkyl chain and bis(perfluorobutylsulfonyl)amide (BPFB) anions bearing double-sided perfluoroalkyl chains were employed to readily replace the hexafluoroantimonate (HFA) counterions in A/HFA and TPQ/HFA, yielding A/PFB, TPQ/PFB, A/BPFB, and TPQ/BPFB. Compared to the incorporated PFB anions, the BPFB anions more effectively restrict intramolecular motion through anion-π+ and van der Waals interactions, thereby significantly enhancing the fluorescence intensity of the phototheranostic agents─by 50.8-fold and 4.2-fold in A/BPFB nanoparticles (NPs) and TPQ/BPFB NPs compared to their HFA analogues, respectively. Concurrently, TPQ/BPFB NPs with second near-infrared emission demonstrated superior ROS generation, excellent mitochondrial targeting, and remarkable resistance to photobleaching. Strikingly, TPQ/BPFB NPs can activate both necroptosis and ferroptosis under irradiation, triggering a robust systemic immune response. Additionally, the lipophilicity granted by BPFB enables TPQ/BPFB NPs to infiltrate deeper into tumors, guaranteeing a more extensive photodynamic therapy with a 95% tumor suppression rate. Crucially, the immune memory triggered by TPQ/BPFB NPs effectively decreases the occurrence of lung metastases. Altogether, the perfluoroalkyl anion strategy proposed in this study offers new insights for developing potent anion-π+ PSs.

item.title: JACS: MetallopeptiGELs: Injectable Short-Peptide Supramolecular Hydrogels Self-Assembled by Pd Nanosheets for Bioorthogonal Therapy
item.description:
Rafael Contreras-Montoya, Maria Sancho-Albero, Catherine Adam, Federico Movilla, Mari C. Mañas-Torres, Modesto T. López-López, Angel Orte, Victor Sebastian, et al.
Controlling the delivery of chemotherapy to the tumor site is a long-standing goal of the medical field, as it could not only enhance the anticancer activity of the treatment but also reduce damage to the rest of the body. The emergence of bioorthogonal catalysis as a strategy capable of mediating continuous drug production in a nonenzymatic fashion has created the opportunity to develop so-called “bioorthogonal therapies,” which aim to generate the anticancer agents inside the tumors. Herein, we describe a novel class of supramolecular materials comprising ultrathin palladium nanosheets and fluorenylmethoxycarbonyl-diphenylalanine that self-assemble in water to form injectable, self-healing, biocompatible catalytic gels that convert inactive prodyes and prodrugs into active small molecules. The relatively weak physicochemical cross-links generated by the hybrid metal-peptide fibers facilitate the flow of the gel under mild shear stress (shear-thinning), thereby enabling precise intratumoral injections in vivo and localized prodrug activation. The strategy was validated in an aggressive pancreatic cancer xenograft model in mice, setting out a new direction for the field of bioorthogonal therapies.

item.title: ACS Nano: Poly(acrylamido) PEG-Alternative Lipids Rescue mRNA Efficacy during Repeated Dosing and Enhance Immune Cell Delivery
item.description:
Benjamin M. Fiedler, Charlotte Galley, Margarita Strimaite, Nga Man Cheng, Najet Mahmoudi, Zhiping Feng, Tammy L. Kalber, Maria-Jose Martinez-Bravo, et al.
Following the successes of the messenger RNA (mRNA) lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccines against COVID-19, mRNA-LNPs are being explored for varied multidose applications including cancer immunotherapies and protein replacement therapies. LNPs rely on poly(ethylene glycol)-lipid (PEG-lipid) coatings for stability, but increasing anti-PEG antibody prevalence threatens repeat-dose efficacy and increases pseudoallergic risk, creating an urgent need for alternatives. Here, we introduce poly(acrylamido) lipids (PAM-lipids), a family of polymer lipids that effectively replace PEG-lipids in mRNA-LNP formulations. Systematic variation of monomer chemistry, molar mass, and end group reveals critical structure–activity relationships determining LNP size, polydispersity, and transfection efficiency. Varying PAM monomer chemistry allows minimization of antipolymer antibody cross-reactivity, with multiple PAM-lipids demonstrating no anti-PEG antibody binding. Several PAM-LNPs exhibit superior mRNA transfection efficacy to PEGylated clinical benchmarks in vitro and in vivo across multiple cell types, organs, routes of administration, and mRNA cargos. In particular, lead PAM-LNPs enhance mRNA delivery to dendritic cells (up to 120-fold in vitro and 3-fold in vivo) and macrophages (4-fold in vivo), with 2.5-fold superior lymph node expression, driven in part by increased cellular association and lymphoid targeting. Crucially, PAM-LNPs evade circulating anti-PEG antibodies to rescue lost mRNA efficacy after repeated dosing, resulting in 300% mRNA expression relative to that of PEG-LNPs. These findings demonstrate PAM-lipids as a chemically varied, immunologically compatible family of PEG alternatives for mRNA-LNP therapeutics.

item.title: JACS: Carbon Insertion into Electron-Deficient (Aza)indoles via a Radical-Polar Crossover Strategy
item.description:
Alexander D. Roth, Ethan E. Hyland, Amelia J. Cook, Tessa Lynch-Colameta, Alec H. Christian, Mark D. Levin
Despite a surge of progress in both strategic approaches and reagent design, carbon insertion into indoles remains limited to electron-rich substrates, notwithstanding the prevalence of electron-poor (aza)indoles in medicinal chemistry. We report herein a radical-polar crossover strategy that overcomes this limitation through a photocatalytic, iodomethyl-radical-mediated cyclopropanation/autoxidation approach. The method enables access to a range of highly substituted, electron-poor quinolines, naphthyridines, and triazanaphthalenes, many of which are challenging to prepare by traditional syntheses. We demonstrate the modification of medicinally relevant (aza)indoles, and preliminary mechanistic observations support autoxidation via an anionic cyclopropane ring opening pathway.

item.title: Nano Letters: Photoinduced Surface Reconstruction Strategy for Enhancing AgBiS2 Quantum Dot Solar Cells
item.description:
Qixuan Zhong, Ruchao Gong, Junxiao Zhang, Lei Xu, Jingzhi Shang, Shuguang Wang, Muhan Cao, Jinxing Chen, et al.
Silver bismuth sulfide (AgBiS2) quantum dots (QDs) are promising candidates for eco-friendly solution-based solar cells. However, structural defects in QDs hinder high efficiency. Controllable synthesis of AgBiS2 QDs remains challenging, often yielding crystals with surface and lattice defects that promote nonradiative recombination. Improving AgBiS2 QD quality before film formation is crucial, as synthesis-related imperfections often persist in devices and inherently limit effective passivation later on. This study presents a photoinduced surface reconstruction method for AgBiS2 QDs that achieves nearly perfect ionic ordering with lower lattice strain, leading to denser films and better band alignment with charge layers than the initial AgBiS2 QDs. Corresponding solar cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 9.71%, exceeding 8.16% for untreated solar cells. By enhancing AgBiS2 QD quality at the source rather than relying solely on downstream passivation, this approach offers a complementary pathway to high-performance QD solar cells.

item.title: JACS: Scalable Fluorinated Copper-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks for Coupled Ultratrace Perfluoroalkyl Substances Monitoring and Efficient Remediation
item.description:
Zhangjie Gu, Yongping Chai, Zhaoyang Jiao, Wenjie Wang, Jiajie Wu, Xiaodong Chi
Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent water contaminants that require both effective removal and reliable monitoring. However, these functions are typically performed separately, preventing real-time evaluation of treatment performance. Here we establish a cooperative host–guest-coupling principle, in which a single host–guest binding event simultaneously drives contaminant capture and modulates the Cu-centered redox process, thereby generating concentration-dependent electrochemical signals within a porous framework. Guided by this principle, we reported a scalable fluorinated copper-based covalent organic framework (F–Cu–COF) synthesized through an open-air one-pot strategy that enables gram-scale production while retaining high crystallinity and chemical stability. Fluorinated pore domains and redox-active Cu centers create a cooperative host–guest environment that promotes PFAS binding and enrichment with electrochemical signal generation. Consequently, F–Cu–COF achieves a detection limit of 5.2 pg L–1, an uptake capacity of 3824 mg g–1, and efficient flow-through removal. This work establishes host–guest coupling as a common molecular basis for linking electrochemical signal generation with contaminant capture in scalable porous materials, providing a general design strategy for multifunctional water-treatment platforms capable of integrated treatment verification.

item.title: JACS: Interhalogen of Iodine Chloride Accelerates Charge Transfer for Efficient Li2O2 Oxidation in Lithium–Oxygen Batteries
item.description:
Jiaxuan An, Yaohui Huang, Lang Zhou, Zhichao Guo, Lin Li, Fujun Li
Li–O2 batteries suffer from sluggish Li2O2 oxidation kinetics at electrode/electrolyte interfaces, leading to large charge polarization and low energy efficiency. Soluble redox mediators (RMs) provide a solution-mediated pathway for Li2O2 decomposition and reduce the charge overpotential. However, the chemical oxidation of Li2O2 by oxidized RMs remains kinetically sluggish, resulting in persistent charge polarization. Herein, iodine monochloride (ICl), an interhalogen compound, is electrochemically generated in situ during the charge process to promote the oxidation of Li2O2. The large electronegativity difference between I and Cl promotes intramolecular charge transfer from I to Cl, creating an electrophilic iodine center (Iδ+) that increases the I–Cl bond polarity and strengthens the interaction with Li2O2. This lowers the decomposition barrier of Li2O2 from 2.39 to 0.77 eV, thereby facilitating its chemical oxidation. The Li–O2 battery delivers a low discharge/charge polarization of 0.52 V, effectively mitigating parasitic reactions at high voltages and enabling an extended cycling lifespan exceeding 800 h. This work provides a valuable design principle for developing redox mediators for efficient Li2O2 oxidation.

item.title: JACS: Support Protection Mechanism Enables Efficient and Stable Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers
item.description:
Kun Li, Chongao Tian, Rui Liu, Yan Guo, Feifei Shi, Ruyue Gao, Xiao Feng, Wenxiu Yang, et al.
Designing oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts that simultaneously achieve high activity and long-term stability remains a critical challenge for the development of alkaline anion exchange membrane water electrolyzers (AEMWEs). Here, we uncover a unique support protection mechanism in which lattice-confined ruthenium (Ru) single atoms offer robust protection for the spinel Co3O4 support, realizing outstanding stability in AEMWEs. Theoretical calculations and structural characterizations reveal that lattice confinement promotes the formation of robust Ru–O–Co bridges by simultaneously shortening the Co–O and Ru–O bond lengths, thereby suppressing Co dissolution and optimizing the electronic structure for efficient catalysis. Furthermore, in situ electrochemical analysis demonstrates that the lattice confinement of Ru atoms accelerates OER kinetics through facilitated proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) steps and partially activated lattice oxygen. As a result, the RuLCA-Co3O4 dominated by the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) exhibits a lower overpotential of 260 mV at 10 mA cm–2, which is lower than that of RuSCA-Co3O4 dominated by the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) pathway. Meanwhile, the lattice-confined RuLCA-Co3O4 exhibits nearly 9-fold lower Co dissolution compared to surface-coordinated RuSCA-Co3O4 after an accelerated durability test (ADT). Moreover, RuLCA-Co3O4 maintains an outstanding stability for over 1000 h in an AEMWE system with a low degradation rate of 88.1 μV h–1, outperforming RuSCA-Co3O4. This work establishes lattice confinement as an effective strategy to decouple activity-stability trade-offs in alkaline OER and provides a viable design principle for durable AEMWE anodes.

item.title: JACS: Decoupling Dissolution from Water Oxidation at Single-Faceted High-Entropy Perovskite Electrodes
item.description:
Subhajit Bhunia, Esteban D. Gadea, Alessandro R. Mazza, Mohana V. Kante, Gangli Wang, Sheng Dai, Thomas Z. Ward, Valeria Molinero, et al.
High-entropy oxides (HEOs) are promising anode materials for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) due to their wide compositional space and electronic flexibility. However, their electrochemical dissolution and OER remain concurrent, preventing decoupled analysis of dissolution kinetics and stability. Here, we present a combined atomic force microscopy (AFM) and scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM) strategy to decouple lattice dissolution from water oxidation under well-defined reaction conditions. Structurally analogous, atomically flat, single-faceted (001) ABO3 perovskite electrodes, La1–xSrx(Cr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2)O3 with x = 0 and 0.3, serve as model systems to probe dissolution and OER kinetics in acid. Pipet-probed localized cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry reveal that the measured current contains contributions from both OER and lattice dissolution, the latter producing nanoscale dissolution pits beneath the SECCM droplet. By correlating pit-growth kinetics with total OER charge as a function of pulse duration (τ), overpotential (η), and pH, we quantitatively separate dissolution from OER. The proportional scaling between dissolution charge and total charge indicates that OER and dissolution proceed within a common kinetic regime, sharing a common intermediate. A rate-law-based analysis yields the standard dissolution rate constant (kd0 cm/s), transfer coefficient (α), and proton reaction order (b) for the dissolution of the 001 facet of both HEO-P. Our results unravel how aliovalent A-site substitution (30% Sr2+) alters dissolution kinetics, charge partitioning between dissolution and OER, and thickness-dependent stability, thereby enabling quantitative disentangling of the intrinsic activity and stability of HEO electrodes.

item.title: JACS: A Pseudo-Icosahedral RhH2Au10 Superatom: Two Hydrogen Atoms Acting as Gold-Atom Equivalents and Modifiers
item.description:
Haru Hirai, Shinjiro Takano, Shinya Masuda, Tatsuya Tsukuda
A hydrogen atom is known to act as a gold-atom-equivalent dopant in gold nanoclusters (AuNCs) by contributing to the valence electron count. To gain insights into the interaction of multiple H atoms with AuNCs, we herein synthesized a di-H-atom-doped NC, [RhH2Au10(dppp)5]3+ (RhH2Au10; dppp = 1,3-bis(diphenylphosphino)propane), by exposing [RhAu10(dppp)5]3+ (RhAu10) to H2 gas; RhAu10 was generated in situ via hydride (H–) abstraction from [RhHAu10(dppp)5]2+. Comprehensive characterization of RhH2Au10 by X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, and theoretical calculations revealed that the two H atoms occupy the two “missing” Au sites in the arachno-type RhAu10 core via dissociative adsorption of H2, forming a pseudo-icosahedral RhH2Au10 core. This core structure contrasts sharply with the previously reported di-H-atom-doped silver- or copper-based superatoms, in which the H atoms form an MH2 (M = Os, Ru, Rh) unit completely encapsulated within an icosahedral Ag12 or Cu12 shell. The RhH2Au10 core possesses an 8-electron closed-shell electronic configuration of (1S)2(1P)6, which is isoelectronic to the icosahedral RhAu12 superatom, thereby demonstrating the Au-atom equivalence of H atoms. Nevertheless, the two H atoms in the RhH2Au10 superatomic core act as structural modifiers compared to the RhAu12 superatom: (1) the degeneracy of the 1P orbitals is lifted by lowering the geometric symmetry, and (2) the HOMO–LUMO energy gap is expanded due to the reduced electronic confinement volume. This study demonstrates that multiple H atoms in a gold-based superatomic core not only behave as Au-atom equivalents but also serve as key components for modulating their fundamental properties.

item.title: ACS Nano: Divide and Conquer Strategy Using Piezoelectric Nanofiber Scaffolds for Stage-Specific Delivery of Bone-Targeted Exosome Mimetics with Ago/AntagomiR-126
item.description:
Jeong In Kim, Subin Park, Soonchul Lee
Bone regeneration is a temporally regulated process requiring stage-specific biochemical cues and biomechanical stimulation; however, current scaffold-based delivery systems largely rely on passive release and fail to adapt to the dynamic healing phases. While previous PVDF-based scaffolds have focused on enhancing piezoelectric output or osteoconductive properties, they primarily function as passive materials without the dynamic regulation of therapeutic activity. Here, we present a multifunctional piezoelectric scaffold that enables mechanically triggered, temporally controlled delivery of bone-targeted exosome mimetics (EMs) loaded with AgomiR or AntagomiR-126. The scaffold features a three-dimensional piezoelectric architecture that generates electromechanical activation under physiological loading, allowing for coupling between mechanical stimulation and therapeutic release. In addition, these components are functionally integrated to coordinate phase-specific miRNA activity during the repair. Alendronate-functionalized EMs enable bone-selective localization, while AgomiR-126 promotes early angiogenesis and progenitor recruitment and AntagomiR-126 enhances late-stage osteogenic differentiation. In vivo studies demonstrated that this system significantly improved bone repair. Rather than introducing a new component, this work establishes a mechanically gated, temporally programmed miRNA delivery strategy for phase-specific bone regeneration.

item.title: Nano Letters: Pixelated Tellurium Nanowire Assemblies for Flexible and Polarization-Driven Multimodal Anticounterfeiting
item.description:
Yingtao Zhao, Hao Liu, Jiajun Liu, Shiyu Liu, Zhenhua Yang, Jinshi Zhao, Jian Zhu
Anticounterfeiting technologies capable of enabling both visual authentication and machine-readable encryption are critically demanded. Here we present a wafer-scale and flexible tellurium nanowire (TeNW) platform with programmable localized orientation, enabling dual-mode anticounterfeiting based on polarization-encoded information. By employing a lock–shear and lift-off strategy, pixelated and highly aligned TeNW arrays with feature sizes down to 5 μm are realized on arbitrary rigid and flexible substrates, exhibiting dichroic ratios of up to 4.6 and stretchability exceeding 100%. Beyond passive optical security, the semiconducting nature of TeNWs allows these oriented arrays to function as active channels in asymmetric Schottky photodetectors, delivering broadband photoresponse (405–1064 nm), an anisotropic photocurrent ratio of 2.35, and an ultrafast response time of 430 μs under self-powered operation. Leveraging this capability, polarization-encoded information can be transduced into polarization-sensitive electrical signals, establishing a hardware-level security paradigm that physically encodes information in the material rather than in algorithms.

item.title: JACS: Enhancing Propanol Production from CO2 Reduction with a Terbium-Doped Copper Nitride Electrocatalyst
item.description:
Hong Phong Duong, Jose Guillermo Rivera de la Cruz, Nicolas Menguy, Quentin Arnoux, Candice Perou, Michael Walls, Domenico Grammatico, Ngoc-Huan Tran, et al.
Propanol is one of the most complex products obtained from CO2 electroreduction (CO2R). Being an interesting precursor for synthetic fuels and a feedstock for the chemical industry, its electrochemical production has recently raised increasing interest. However, low selectivity for propanol has been achieved so far. Here, via exploring a variety of original lanthanide-doped copper nitride materials, we identified and characterized terbium-doped copper nitride as the most selective catalyst for propanol formation. It allowed CO2R to yield propanol with a Faradaic efficiency of 27% at a high current density of 300 mA cm–2 within a neutral (KHCO3 electrolyte) flow cell, surpassing the performance of previous CO2R catalysts. The high density of undercoordinated nitride-derived Cu sites, combined with the increased oxophilicity of the surface, likely promoted the selectivity toward alcohols. Thorough DFT calculations showed that Tb doping increased the affinity for oxygenate-associated C2* intermediates and lowered the free-energy barrier for reactions coupling the latter with CO* toward propanol.

item.title: JACS: Layer-Distortion Engineering of Acridinium-Based Covalent Organic Frameworks Enables Efficient Photoredox Transformations of Alcohols
item.description:
Yimin Pan, Shufang Tang, Wenyu Li, Ailin Pan, Yifan Dong, Wenbin Lin, Haifeng Zheng
Planar two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) often suffer from severe interlayer π–π stacking, which promotes excitonic recombination, restricts access to active sites, and compromises photocatalytic efficiency. Here we report a layer-distortion engineering strategy to construct wavy acridinium-based COFs, Mes-Acr-TAPB and Mes-Acr-TAPP, by introducing structural distortion into otherwise planar layered frameworks. The resulting wavy framework efficiently suppresses interlayer π–π stacking, enlarges interlayer spacing, modulates molecular packing, pore environment, and improves accessibility to photoactive acridinium sites. Compared with the planar analog Dur-Acr-TAPB, Mes-Acr-TAPB exhibits enhanced exciton dissociation along with substrate absorption, more efficient charge separation, and superior photocatalytic activity. As a heterogeneous photoredox catalyst, Mes-Acr-TAPB enables diverse alcohol transformations under mild conditions, including β-scission radical functionalization, ring contraction/expansion, and skeletal transposition. Mes-Acr-TAPB shows broad functional-group tolerance and supports late-stage structural modification of complex natural products, highlighting its synthetic utility. This work establishes layer-distortion as an effective design principle for mitigating interlayer stacking in 2D COFs and advancing high-performance COF photocatalysts for sustainable organic synthesis.

item.title: JACS: Kinetic Control of Polymorphism in Li10.5Si1.5P1.5S12–Based Solid Electrolytes
item.description:
Jingui Yang, Ramon Zimmermanns, Maik Schmitt, Torsten Brezesinski, Florian Strauss
Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS)-type solid electrolytes (SEs) are among the most promising materials for next-generation solid-state batteries (SSBs) due to their high lithium-ion conductivity. However, challenges related to phase stability and polymorphism, especially in Ge-free, Si-based systems, limit their practical implementation. Here, the crystallization and phase transition behavior of materials with a nominal composition of Li10.5–xSi1.5P1.5S12–xIx (x = 0, 0.2, 0.4) are systematically investigated. Operando high-temperature synchrotron X-ray diffraction, total scattering with pair distribution function analysis, and differential scanning calorimetry measurements reveal the formation of a metastable orthorhombic (o) phase, followed by transformation into the thermodynamically stable tetragonal (t) phase at elevated temperatures. Our findings indicate that lithium iodide (LiI) as an additive regulates the crystallization of the o-phase and thereby governs the transition kinetics. This enables the o-to-t phase transition to occur at much reduced temperatures and faster rates. Neutron powder diffraction further uncovers minor modifications to the Si/P ratio and lithium sublattice, as well as the fact that iodine is not incorporated into the t-phase; instead, a secondary Li4PS4I-type phase forms. Collectively, this work highlights the critical role of microstructural engineering on crystallization and polymorphism in LGPS-type SEs and also demonstrates the applicability of these dual-phase materials by enabling high-performance lithium–sulfur SSBs.

item.title: Nano Letters: Unveiling the Creep Recovery Behavior of Pseudo-Free-Standing Polymer Thin Films for Wearable Electronics
item.description:
Eun Sung Oh, Dong Jun Kim, Won Choi, Taek-Soo Kim
Polymer thin films in wearable electronics undergo creep recovery during operation as on-body devices, resulting in unrecoverable strain that subsequently induces mechanical instability in the films. However, the creep recovery behavior of polymer thin films has not been investigated due to their intrinsic fragility and the difficulty in controlling ultralow loads for the films. We evaluate the creep recovery behavior of pseudo-free-standing polymer thin films as a function of creep stress, developing direct creep recovery testing with a feedback-based ultralow-load control system. Polystyrene (PS) thin films exhibit a sharp increase in unrecoverable strain with the onset of crazing. While poly(3-butylthiophene) (P3BT) thin films show a linear increase in the relative ratio of unrecoverable strain with increasing creep stress, poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT) thin films exhibit a viscoelastic strain larger than unrecoverable strain. This work reveals the creep recovery behavior of polymer thin films and proposes a direct creep recovery testing method.

item.title: JACS: Efficient Chemical Synthesis and Enzymatic Replication of 3′-Deoxyapionucleic Acid (ApioNA): An RNA-Selective XNA with Conformational Flexibility
item.description:
Chenghe Xiong, Chunlei Zhang, Lei He, Xianfei Zhang, Yihang Gao, Junlin Wen, Congmin Liu, Lu Zhou, et al.
Xeno-nucleic acids (XNAs) have emerged as versatile platforms due to their sugar scaffolds that enable precise chemical tuning, leading to distinct classes ranging from fully compatible systems to orthogonal systems. However, sugar-modified XNAs capable of discriminating between RNA and DNA have remained elusive. In this work, we establish 3′-deoxyapionucleic acid (ApioNA) as a structurally flexible XNA with inherent RNA-selective hybridization properties. We achieved efficient production of ApioNA oligonucleotides through an efficient asymmetric synthesis of their building blocks and systematically characterized their properties. Thermal melting analyses demonstrate that ApioNA forms moderately stable duplexes with RNA while exhibiting weak pairing with DNA and negligible self-association. Quantum mechanical calculations reveal that the apiofuranose ring populates two low-energy puckering states, and the addition of an extra methylene group enhances backbone flexibility, thereby favoring A-form geometry for RNA pairing while requiring a higher-energy state to accommodate B-form DNA. Despite its weak affinity for DNA, ApioNA supports a complete enzymatic replication cycle using commercial Therminator and Bst 3.0 polymerases with approximately 98% fidelity and is processed by native E. coli machinery in vivo. This work fills the RNA-selective niche in the XNA functional landscape and establishes sugar puckering dynamics and backbone flexibility as key design principles for programming nucleic acid pairing specificity.

item.title: JACS: Electrochemical Synthesis of Slaked Lime Utilizing a Diaphragm Flow Cell
item.description:
J. Gage Wright, Jason W. Misleh, Nawal M. Alghoraibi, Matthew W. Kanan
Slaked lime (Ca(OH)2) is one of the most widely utilized chemicals, with applications in diverse industries including construction, mining, water treatment, and chemical manufacturing. Currently, Ca(OH)2 is synthesized by coal-fired calcination of CaCO3 to make CaO, followed by exothermic hydration. Converting CaCO3 into Ca(OH)2 using electrochemically generated acid and base has attracted great interest because it could be powered by renewable electricity and would generate the CO2 byproduct in a pure form. Previous electrochemical Ca(OH)2 syntheses have incorporated the processing of calcium salts within the electrochemical cell to avoid acid–base recombination losses, but these cells have poor stability and high energy demand. Herein, we show that production of high-salinity acid and base solutions using a diaphragm flow cell (DFC) coupled with ex situ processing of CaCO3 substantially improves the efficiency of electrochemical Ca(OH)2 production. Using a closed loop with a simple KCl salt solution, we demonstrate the synthesis of >99% pure Ca(OH)2 for 0.088 to 0.10 kWh per mole at productive current densities of 158 to 334 mA cm–2.

item.title: JACS: Boosting Ionomer Oxygen Transport via Pore Confinement in Carbon Supports for Low-Pt Fuel Cells
item.description:
Pengyu Song, Zhaojing Ni, Xiaotao Liu, Cailin Xiao, Lin Zeng, Bo Wang, Lu Wang
Low-Pt proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are promising for hydrogen energy implementation, yet oxygen transport through ionomer-covered catalyst surfaces becomes increasingly limiting due to the resistance associated with dense ionomer films. Herein, we demonstrate a pore-confinement strategy to manipulate the spatial locality of Pt nanoparticles within porous carbon supports, enabling simultaneous regulation of ionomer distribution and molecular organization. Pt nanoparticles were selectively positioned on the external surfaces (Ptext/PC) or within the internal nanopores (Ptint/PC) of otherwise comparable supports, while maintaining similar Pt loading, particle size, and pore characteristics. Under H2-air condition, Ptint/PC delivered a peak power density ∼1.3 times higher than that of Ptext/PC, but a similar current density in the high-voltage region. Electrochemical analyses reveal that the performance enhancement originates from improved oxygen transport rather than catalytic activity. Wide-angle X-ray scattering and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the Pt nanoparticles confined within mesopores disrupt the dense packing of ionomer backbones, thereby boosting oxygen permeability at the catalyst–ionomer interface. By establishing a direct relationship between Pt locality, ionomer distribution, backbone organization, and oxygen transport, this work identifies catalyst locality as an effective parameter for engineering interfacial mass transport and provides a new design principle for low-Pt PEMFCs.

item.title: JACS: Synthetic W/Cu Mimics of the Mo/Cu Active Site in Aerobic CODH: Nonclassical Isocyanide Coordination and the Role of the Bridging Sulfide
item.description:
Mahesh Kumar Choudhary, Daniel Kim, Neal P. Mankad
Aerobic carbon monoxide dehydrogenase (CODH) uses an unsupported Mo–S–Cu heterobimetallic active site to catalyze CO oxidation, but the mechanistic role of the bridging sulfide remains to be fully resolved. We report a series of W/Cu complexes designed to test whether steric shielding from a bidentate tBuxantphos ligand can suppress unwanted Cu···Sdithiolate and Cu···O═M interactions that plagued the reactivity of a previously reported NHC-ligated model system. Addition of [Cu(tBuxantphos)]+ to [(bdt)WVI(O)(OSiiPr3)(X)]− (bdt = 1,2-benzenedithiolate; X = O, S, Se) unexpectedly favors Cu coordination at the W═O rather than the W═X unit, giving X═W–O–Cu cores as the thermodynamically preferred isomers, opposite to the connectivity predicted by hard–soft acid–base theory and found in CODH itself. The resulting complexes bind isocyanides at CuI with nonclassical (blue-shifted) C≡N stretching frequencies. In contrast, no reactivity is observed toward CO gas, consistent with DFT predictions that CO coordination is endergonic. However, the calculations reveal that the CO adduct of the hypothetical O═W–S–Cu–CO isomer is more stabilized than its S═W–O–Cu–CO counterpart, an effect traced by molecular orbital analysis to delocalization of electron density from the redox-active dithiolate through the bridging sulfide into the Cu–CO π-backbonding manifold. These results provide an electronic rather than purely structural rationale for why the CODH active site retains a bridging sulfide despite an apparent thermodynamic preference for a bridging oxo in the synthetic analogues investigated here.

item.title: ACS Nano: Effect of Chiral-Induced Spin Selectivity in Half-Metallic La0.67Sr0.33MnO3 Thin Films
item.description:
Michal Bennár, Marianna Španková, Štefan Chromik, Marcel Talacko, Iuliia Vetrova, Andrej Dvurečenskij, Alexander Cigáň, Martin Škrátek, et al.
Magnetism induced by the proximity effects of chiral molecules is a physical phenomenon that can be demonstrated with molecular layers as thin as 1 nm deposited on thin films of conventional ferromagnets. Although the chiral-induced spin selectivity effect has been widely explored in the context of spintronic applications involving charge transport through chiral molecules, due to its capacity to generate high spin polarizations at room temperature, the accompanying process of induced magnetization without applied current likewise presents opportunities for exploitation. In this work, we demonstrate that, unlike conventional ferromagnets, where the induced magnetization aligns with the chiral axis of the polymer, the CISS effect in half-metallic ferromagnets (La0.67Sr0.33MnO3) favors a quasi-perpendicular magnetization configuration. This preference for quasi-perpendicular magnetization is caused by the formation of a thermally driven steady state, which, due to different transport probabilities into the molecule, results in a modification of the domain-wall energy landscape. These results provide insight into the chiral-induced spin selectivity effect without net currents and also clarify mechanism for controlling magnetization within half-metallic thin films for spintronic devices.

item.title: JACS: Intricate Proteoform Heterogeneity in the Tailpiece of IgA within and across Its Circulatory and Secretory Configurations
item.description:
Weiwei Wang, Amber D. Rolland, Gestur Vidarsson, Johannes B. van Goudoever, Karli R. Reiding, Albert Bondt, Albert J. R. Heck
Human immunoglobulin A (IgA) naturally occurs in multiple molecular forms─monomers, dimers, and even higher-order polymers─that are differentially distributed across serum, breast milk, and mucosal surfaces. The C-terminal tailpiece of IgA is essential to its polymerization mediated by the joining chain (J-chain) and thus also an important determinant of its extensive structural heterogeneity, yet its features remain somewhat poorly defined. Here, we used HILIC-LC-MS/MS-based glycopeptide analysis to characterize the N-glycan structures, disulfide linkages, and C-terminal amino acid sequence variants within the IgA tailpiece across the different molecular configurations of endogenous IgA. We find extensive correlation between these post-translational modifications; i.e., variations in tailpiece Asn459 N-glycosylation, redox status and disulfide connectivity of Cys471, and the presence or absence of C-terminal Tyr472 are intrinsically interconnected. When Cys471 was disulfide-bound to the J-chain, Asn459 glycans showed broader structural heterogeneity and retained more high-mannose structures, whereas free Cys471 tailpieces mainly carried mature, sialylated complex-type glycans. Serum IgA and milk SIgA displayed distinct tailpiece signatures, including differences in N-glycan maturation and processing of the ultimate C-terminal Tyr472 residue. Together, these findings define biofluid-specific molecular forms of IgA and highlight the remarkable structural diversity of the human IgA tailpiece. Overall, our results advance the understanding of the IgA structure and could offer a much-needed molecular basis to assist future bioengineering of IgA-based therapeutics.

item.title: JACS: A Microporous Zr-Tetraphosphonate MOF with Permanent Porosity, Robustness, and Thermochemical Heat Storage Capability
item.description:
Pablo Salcedo-Abraira, Catalina Biglione, Sérgio M. F. Vilela, Artem A. Babaryk, Antonio Rodríguez-Diéguez, Philippe Trens, Fabrice Salles, Jerzy Zajac, et al.
Combining high-valent metal cations with phosphonate linkers represents a promising strategy to address the limited stability of MOFs, yet permanently porous phosphonate MOFs (P-MOFs) remain rare due to the strong coordination propensity of phosphonate groups. Herein, we report IEF-10, a new microporous zirconium tetraphosphonate framework constructed from ZrO5F octahedral secondary building units and a pyrene tetraphosphonate linker. The material combines three features that are seldom achieved simultaneously in P-MOFs: permanent accessible microporosity (equivalent BET surface area ∼430 m2·g–1), accessible phosphonic acid functionalities (-PO3H), and exceptional thermal (up to 450 °C), mechanical (>3 tons), and chemical stability (pH 1–12, organic solvents). The structure exhibits reversible water adsorption with moderate uptake and experimentally determined capacities of heat storage of ∼400–500 J·g–1, reflecting a favorable balance between host–guest interactions and regeneration requirements. As a proof of concept, IEF-10 was evaluated for thermochemical heat storage under dynamic moist-gas flow conditions. Calorimetric measurements revealed fast heat-release kinetics (3–4 h), and excellent cyclability in terms of heat release (at least 10 cycles, total test duration of 5 weeks). The hydrophobic surface character is an advantage for long-term storage uses as the adsorbent can remain in a dry state between the charging and discharging stages even at low relative humidity levels in the reactor. These results demonstrate how the combination of permanent porosity, accessible phosphonic acid groups, and exceptional framework robustness can enable functional adsorption-driven energy storage while providing new opportunities for the development of porous zirconium P-MOFs.

item.title: JACS: Fluorine-Mediated Molten-Salt Crystallization Regulates Phase Evolution and Structural Stability in Sodium Layered Oxides
item.description:
Chenguang Shi, Junyi Yao, Xiaowen Zhan, Jeongok Choe, Xixian Yang, He Zhou, Amir Ashraf Elnashar, Rupayan Ghosh, et al.
Ni- and Co-free P2-type Fe–Mn layered oxides with high Na concentrations are promising cathodes for sodium-ion batteries, but their practical use is limited by phase instability during Na-excess synthesis and structural degradation during cycling and storage. Although large single-crystal-like architectures could improve stability, controlled phase-selective crystallization in these cathode systems remains challenging. Here, we show that fluorine-assisted molten-salt synthesis enables controlled formation of large-particle Fe–Mn–Ti P2 cathodes with enhanced phase selectivity and structural coherence. Compared with Na-excess processing alone, NaF-assisted flux growth expands the P2 phase stability window and promotes large particles with uniform morphologies while preserving local layered ordering. Multiscale characterization further reveals more-reversible structural evolution and more homogeneous Mn redox behavior in the NaF-assisted material, together with a gradient-like fluorine distribution involving surface-enriched NaF-like species and lower level interior fluorine environments. These coupled structural, morphological, and chemical features collectively mitigate crack formation and deliver good cycling stability. In summary, NaF-assisted molten-salt synthesis shows promise in addressing key limitations of Ni- and Co-free P2-type Fe–Mn layered cathodes.

item.title: JACS: G-Quadruplex-Interacting Photooxidative Platinum(IV) Prodrug for Inhibiting Oncogene Transcription and Amplifying Antitumor Immunity
item.description:
Dengshuai Wei, Yijia Chen, Jiaqian Xu, Guangyu Zhu
Conventional platinum (Pt)-based chemotherapeutics elicit cancer cell death primarily through DNA binding, but this approach is inherently limited by poor site specificity and a lack of spatiotemporal control, which compromises therapeutic precision and safety. To overcome these limitations, we report DNATplatin, an in situ activatable and photooxidative Pt(IV) prodrug designed to combine precise recognition of DNA secondary structures with targeted genetic intervention through DNA photooxidation. By incorporating a bis-N-methylpyridinium moiety to selectively recognize DNA, DNATplatin shows a 10-fold increase in the levels in genomic DNA relative to oxaliplatin and a 2.5-fold emission turn-on selectivity for G-quadruplexes (G4s) over typical duplex DNA. Following precise nuclear localization, photoactivated DNATplatin acts as a potent photooxidant that oxidizes G4, dismantles G4 scaffolds, and abrogates circular dichroism signatures. These orchestrated lesions generate localized oxidative stress and selectively silence major G4-driven oncogenes, thereby effectively circumventing traditional Pt resistance by bypassing canonical adduct-dependent pathways. In a murine triple-negative breast tumor model, DNATplatin produces profound tumor suppression and elicits a robust systemic immune response, characterized by CD4+/CD8+ T-cell activation and depletion of Foxp3+ regulatory T cells. Collectively, this work establishes a controllable “target-and-destroy” strategy and underscores the potential of Pt(IV) photooxidants for topology-selective genetic intervention.

item.title: Nano Letters: Unidirectional Magnetoresistance Driven by Nonequilibrium Antiferromagnetic Magnons
item.description:
Xue He, Hans Gløckner Giil, Caiqiong Xu, Jicheng Wang, Arne Brataas, Jinbo Yang, Yanglong Hou, Zhaochu Luo, et al.
Magnetoresistive effects are typically symmetric under magnetization reversal. However, nonlinear spin transport can give rise to unidirectional magnetoresistance in systems with strong spin–orbit interaction and broken inversion symmetry. Here, we report a large magnonic unidirectional spin Hall magnetoresistance (USMR) in a van der Waals antiferromagnet CrPS4 in contact with Pt, driven by the nonequilibrium magnon accumulation with a finite magnon chemical potential. In contrast to conventional magnonic USMR driven by magnetization fluctuations, this effect persists under strong magnetic fields and low temperatures. The magnitude of magnonic USMR in CrPS4/Pt exceeds that of YIG/Pt by more than 2 orders of magnitude and surpasses the electrical USMR in metallic Ta/Co bilayers by a factor of 2. Our results highlight magnon chemical potential gradients for nonlinear magnetoresistance in antiferromagnetic van der Waals heterostructures and open a route to magnon-based antiferromagnetic spintronic functionalities in two-terminal device geometries.
